Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Apex Medical Devices Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jennifer Hale, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Moreno, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Medical Devices demonstrated significant progress this quarter, driven by our focus on innovation, operational excellence, and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover seven key aspects of our performance:
1. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year
2. Organic revenue growth by segment and geography
3. FDA approvals and CE marks obtained
4. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives
5. Key assumptions underlying the guidance
6. Capital equipment vs consumables mix trends
7. Strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter

Jennifer will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Patel will offer insights into our technology roadmap, and Lisa will discuss our commercial strategies. Afterwards, we'll open the call for your questions.

Let's kick off with one of our standout achievements this quarter: aspect 3, our FDA approvals and CE marks obtained. These regulatory milestones represent some of the most transformative wins in our 15-year history, positioning us to grab substantial share in the $28 billion global structural heart market and the $12 billion neuromodulation segment. They're not just regulatory hurdles cleared—they're true revenue accelerators that highlight our disciplined innovation approach and de-risk our trajectory toward sustained double-digit growth.

On the FDA side, we notched three 510(k) clearances and one pivotal PMA approval in Q3, pushing our year-to-date total to eight—60% ahead of last year. This ramp-up comes from leaning into the FDA's Breakthrough Devices Program, where two flagship products now hold designations. Leading is our AetherFlex TAVR system, a next-gen transcatheter aortic valve replacement platform featuring integrated 4D imaging and AI-driven deployment analytics. PMA approval came on September 15th after an 18-month review—faster than the usual 24-30 months for Class III devices—greenlighting full U.S. commercialization in Q4. IDE trial results showed 92% procedural success and 35% lower paravalvular leak versus predicates like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien 3 Ultra. We're eyeing $250 million in U.S. TAVR revenue for FY2025, scaling to $450 million by FY2026, targeting over 150,000 annual U.S. procedures needing better low-profile options.

Supporting that, our PulseGuard ICD—a leadless implantable cardioverter-defibrillator with subcutaneous bio-sensing and Bluetooth Low Energy remote monitoring—earned 510(k) clearance on August 22nd. It meets surging 20% annual demand for MRI-conditional, leadless tech amid climbing infection rates of 2-3% per implant per ACC guidelines. We've secured letters of intent from 15 major IDNs like Kaiser Permanente and Cleveland Clinic, aiming for 12,000 units in Year 1 at $28,000 ASP—yielding $336 million potential with over 75% gross margins via our nitinol processing and ASIC design integration.

Rounding out FDA wins, the NeuroLink DBS array for Parkinson's and essential tremor got 510(k) under De Novo with cybersecurity upgrades per the FDA's 2023 digital health roadmap. Its adaptive algorithms tweak stimulation in real-time based on local field potentials, cutting battery draw 40% versus Medtronic's Percept PC, tapping a $3.2 billion U.S. market growing at 15% CAGR per Grand View Research.

For CE marks, we landed five Class III certifications under the tough EU MDR, standing out amid transition delays hitting 40% of legacy devices. MDR was our priority, with $45 million spent on biocompatibility testing per ISO 10993-1 and EUDAMED v3.0 surveillance. The AetherFlex TAVR CE mark via BSI on July 10th—six months ahead of peers thanks to hybrid U.S. IDE data—unlocks €180 million in EU revenue over 24 months, focusing on Germany's and France's 45,000 annual TAVR volumes. PulseGuard ICD followed on August 5th, outlasting Boston Scientific's Emblem S-ICD with 12-year battery life from DFMA-optimized power tech.

U.S. approvals drive 70% of pipeline speed, boosted by FDA staffing gains post-Inflation Reduction Act. Europe's MDR challenges open doors—our perfect submission timing gives first-mover edge in the €4.5 billion EU CRM market. These feed China NMPA and Japan PMDA filings, aiming for 25% APAC revenue mix by FY2027.

These de-risk our 3-5 year view. Q3 R&D at 14% of revenue ($112 million) targeted SaMD integration—our TAVR AI as IMDRF Level 2—and NIST 800-53 cybersecurity. Modular platforms cut time-to-market 28% and NRE 22%. Four more 510(k)s and two PMAs in review, plus robotic EndoShield for AFib ablation. Partnerships with Philips on imaging and Terumo in Asia amplify. Overall, these fuel 25-30% Devices segment growth, lifting TAM penetration to 8% in structural heart, with 200bps gross margin expansion to 68%.

With that regulatory momentum, let's turn to our strategic priorities and focus areas for next quarter, aspect 7. These will drive our full-year guidance of 11-13% organic growth and 150bps EBITDA expansion to 28-29%. Q3 hit $1.28 billion revenue, up 12% organic from 15% structural heart procedures and ortho share gains, but Q4 demands intense execution on three pillars: innovation acceleration, geographic expansion, and operational excellence.

First, ramping high-growth products. Q3 R&D was $285 million, 22% of revenue—matching Intuitive Surgical and Edwards Lifesciences. Q4 launches full U.S. commercialization of NeoFlex TAVR, beating PULSE trial endpoints with 2.8% one-year mortality vs. 3.5% benchmark. FDA approval in late September targets 8,000 Q4 implants, hitting 15% U.S. share from 9% via self-expanding nitinol reducing leaks under 4%. AI-Enabled NeuroStim advances to Phase III for migraine with 65% responders, outpacing Medtronic's Evolve; $50 million Q4 capex scales Galway manufacturing for $75 million FY2025 revenue. PrecisionOrtho robotic arm gets V1.5 AI kinematics software, eyeing 20% knee adoption amid 35% U.S. ASC ortho shift. Tailwinds: 7-9% global procedures in 2025, 12% structural heart CAGR, 15% robotics.

Second, geographic expansion. U.S. (58% Q3 revenue) leverages stable CMS 2025 fees despite 2.8% cut, targeting 14% growth with 500 NeoFlex trainings vs. Abbott Navitor. Europe (25%) hits 18% via PrecisionOrtho CE renewals in DACH, €20 million distributor investments like Boston Scientific. APAC (28% Q3 YoY) gets $100 million: China JV with Mindray ramps NeoFlex to 2,000 procedures (10% share in 20% market); Japan Shonin for NeuroStim unlocks ¥5 billion; India EchoGuard wearable (40% below iRhythm) yields 92% diagnostics in 500 million underserved. LATAM/MENA add 5% via Mexico tariffs and UAE zones.

Third, operational excellence. Value Engineering 2.0 saves $45 million (10% from TAVR design); inventory to 285 days, working capital 18% sales for 200bps FCF to 22%. Scope 3 emissions down 15% with recycled rare earths, earning DJSI spot for ESG flows. Hiring 250 engineers in Minneapolis/Singapore, 10% above Stryker comps vs. 25% vacancy.

Q4 revenue $1.35-1.38 billion (12-14% organic), structural heart +20%, ortho +10%; EBITDA $380-395 million (28.5%). Risks: 3% FX, U.S. election on IRA. We're reshaping the $600 billion medtech market.

I'll now turn the call over to Jennifer for a deep dive into our financial results, covering revenue guidance, organic growth details, pricing and costs, key guidance assumptions, and capital vs. consumables mix—our remaining aspects 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6.

Jennifer Hale:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we posted strong financial results this quarter, underpinned by these key drivers.

Starting with aspect 2, our organic revenue growth by segment and geography. Excluding our NeuroStim Solutions acquisition and FX headwinds, we delivered 9.2% organic growth year-over-year, up from 7.8% in Q1 and beating our 8% midpoint. This stemmed from 12% above pre-pandemic elective volumes globally, 1-2% ASP gains, and innovation ramps.

By segment—98% of portfolio—Cardiovascular (42%) hit 11.5% organic, led by 15% TAVR volume growth where EvoFlow valve grabbed 250bps share to 28% U.S. per Millennium, structural heart +18% on MitraClip-like repairs, pacemakers/ICDs +8% on Micra leadless with CMS boosts. Orthopedics (25%) reached 10.8%, strongest in three quarters; hip/knee +14% on 20% U.S. vs. 2019 volumes, Mako over 1 million procedures (+22%), 3% ASP from TriFit stems post-supply stabilization. MedSurg/Endoscopy (18%) +7.9%, endoscopy +12% on single-use duodenoscopes (+30% U.S. units vs. FDA reprocessing risks), Phasix bioresorbables +15% offsetting hernia softness. Diabetes/Neuromodulation (15%) +8.4%, CGM FreeStyle Libre +20% APAC, pumps 10% attach, ReviDBS +9% post-COVID with FDA breakthrough.

Geographically, U.S. (76%) led at 10.7% with 300+bps robotics/structural share per NPM, ASC ortho to 45%. EMEA +7.2%, 15% Germany/France TAVR/endoscopy offsetting UK NHS, flat ASPs under MDR. APAC (12%) +12.4%, China +25% ($45 million TAVR), Japan +18% CGM/ortho, India endoscopy double. LATAM/EM +6.1% on Brazil/Mexico.

This validates our Innovate, Penetrate, Expand framework: $450 million half-year R&D for 12 launches like AI endoscopy akin to GI Genius/Viz.ai. Tailwinds: 5-7% medtech CAGR, cardio-ortho demographics, value-based care. Share gains vs. Boston Scientific/Zimmer, pricing intact. Q3 guide 8-10%, accelerating FY25 with Hugo robotics post-CE. Risks: titanium volatility, U.S. reimbursement; 45% margins buffer.

Building on this growth, aspect 1: our Q4 2024 and FY2025 guidance. Wrapping a transformative year, guidance reflects momentum in Cardiovascular, Orthopedics, Neuromodulation from procedure volumes, share gains, innovations—factoring FX headwinds and ex-U.S. pricing.

Q4 total revenue $2.85-2.90 billion, 10-11% reported, 12-13% organic vs. prior $2.80-2.88 billion, on U.S. procedures and next-gen adoption. Cardiovascular (45%): $1.28-1.30 billion, 13-14% organic; EvoClip mitral +25% TAVR attach like Sapien, U.S. procedures +8% vs. 5-6% consensus. Orthopedics (30%): $850-870 million, 9-10%; Mako base >1,200 (+20%), 85% utilization like Stryker, 12% knee share. Neuromodulation (15%): $420-430 million, 15-16%; ReviX DBS +30% rechargeables on Medicare/partners.

Regions: U.S. (60%) 14% organic, $500 million sales force; EMEA (25%) 8%, 2-3pt FX/NHC Germany offset by UK/France 20%; APAC/EM (15%) 10%, China $150 million EvoClip CE.

Margins: GAAP gross 68.5-69.0%, adjusted 70.0-70.5% (+150bps) on Guadalajara 95% utilization, low provisions; adjusted op margin 25.5-26.0% (+100bps YoY) via $100 million OpEx/zero-based/15% R&D-sales; EPS $1.85-1.90 adjusted (+12%).

FY2025: $11.75-11.95 billion, 9-11% reported/10-12% organic; mid-teens high-acuity offset 1-2pt ex-U.S. pricing. Drivers: EvoClip $400 million, Mako AI (+10% util), Infinity SCS like Nevro HF10; $1.2 billion R&D (10%) on TAVR bioresorbables/ML neuromod, NeuroPulse Phase III FDA H1 2025; $1 billion M&A post-RhythmTech, $800 million-1 billion buybacks (2-3% EPS). Segments: Cardio 12%, Ortho 10%, Neuro 14%. Adjusted gross 69.5-70.0% (+200bps) Galway Industry 4.0/resins; op 26.0-26.5% ($300 million savings); EPS $7.60-7.80 (+11-14%). US 13%, EMEA 9%, APAC 12%. 80% FX hedge, 1-2pt recession/regs; 98% PMA rate buffer. Confident in $600 billion medtech at 5-7% CAGR.

Next, aspect 4: impact of pricing and cost management. Key to 8% core organic, 220bps adjusted gross to 68.2%, EBITDA 26.4%—three-year high. Pricing: 2.8% ASP rise (ahead 2-2.5% guide) from mix/contract. Cardio premium stents (like Synergy) 45% revenue (+13% ASP, INSPIRE 4.2% failure vs. 7.1%); 85% GPO renewals with Vizient/Premier, AI bundling vs. 1.9% CMS OPPS. U.S. (52%) +3.4%, Europe (28%) +1.9% value-based neuro (€45 million), EM (20%) -0.5% offset volume. ML pricing tool 88% accurate for FY25 2-3%.

Costs: $162 million sequential savings ($650 million run-rate, 5.2% COGS); 310bps YoY gross expansion, 65% supply/manufacturing. Hedged 70% metals ($28 million save), 95% dual-source, vendors to 850 (-7.8%); Smart Factory Lean Six Sigma +22% throughput Galway, cobots -9.2% labor, 3D knees -32% outsource to 72% margins. R&D $1.42 billion flat but +15% trials via virtual twins (-40% prototypes), 4% headcount save $45 million. U.S. $95 million nearshoring, Europe ESG grants, APAC local 85%.

Margin First: 70%+ gross funds structural heart premiums (TAVR 2.1% stroke vs. 3.8% Sapien); divested wounds $120 million to M&A. Risks: Medicare Advantage, Red Sea; set for 3% ASP, 400bps to 70%+ FY26.

Aspect 6: capital equipment vs. consumables mix. Q3 mix 38% capital/62% consumables, from 42/58% prior; TTM 64% consumables beats 2025 60% target early, +320bps gross to 68.2%, 4pts EPS beat. Capital $148 million +9% YoY, 78 CardioBot Xi placements ($1.9 million ASP), 22 hours/week util +3. Consumables $312 million +18% reported/20% cc, base to 4,200 ($285k pull-through vs. $250k), PCI +22%, ablation +25% AI mapping (+18% efficiency), $1,450 ASP.

Regions: U.S. 65/35 (+14% base, structural), EMEA 16% consumables (MDR capex flat), APAC 45/55 (28 placements China/India Mindray), LATAM 92% attach. Pillars: CardioBot Prime Q4 launch (NVIDIA ML, 30% util lift), Utilization Program 95% attach/24 hours Q4, StenCore $250 million tuck-in (+$80 million 75% margins, $320k pull-through). FY24 consumables 17-19%, capital 10-12%, to 66% mix; $2.45-2.50 billion revenue, 25-27% EBITDA. 95% in-source vs. Biosecure/nitinol risks.

Finally, aspect 5: key assumptions for guidance. FY2024 revenue $2.85-2.95 billion (9-13% reported/10-14% organic), EPS $5.25-5.45 (+12-16%), gross 68-69%, op 24.5-25.5% (+150-200bps).

Assumptions: Procedures mid-single global (4-6% Evaluate/Deloitte), ortho 6-8% U.S. (Apex/Vertex vs. Stryker/Zimmer, CMS +12% joints), cardio 10% TAVR (Sentinel/CardioFlow). U.S. 80% normalized no respurge, Europe 3-5% DRG/France clawbacks, China 15-18% 70% ramp. Pricing flat-+1%: U.S. +2% premium robotics 25% attach offset 1-2% GPO stents, Europe -1% HTA neuro mitigated. Supply: 80% diversified sourcing, 85% resins locked, freight 2%, 4% labor no strikes. R&D $320 million (11.5%) four launches (Vertex AI, Pulse Ablation, Sentinel Ultra 20% less leak), 15-20% TAVR share VISTA data, 8% headcount/12% rep productivity Salesforce. Macro: cc guide, 1-2% FX $25-50 million, Fed 5.25% no recession, 7-9% IDN capex, tax 19-20% FDII. Hedges: 40% ortho ambulatory +20% EndoFlex, IRA credits; risks CMS DRGs 2%, China regs, 3% CPI—200bps EPS conservatism, $300 million buybacks.

These position us to outperform Medtronic/Abbott.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Patel for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Jennifer. We continue to invest in cutting-edge technologies. Our development of the AetherFlex TAVR and NeoFlex platforms is progressing well ahead of schedule, and we anticipate they will revolutionize structural heart interventions by reducing complications and enabling broader adoption in outpatient settings. Similarly, advancements in our ReviX and NeuroLink neuromodulation systems, with adaptive AI algorithms, are set to transform Parkinson's management.

Our R&D spend remains robust at around 14-22% of revenue, fueling modular platforms that cut development times and costs. Phase III trials for NeuroPulse are on track for FDA submission next year, and we're integrating ML-optimized features across robotics like PrecisionOrtho and Mako-inspired systems. Partnerships with NVIDIA and Philips enhance our AI imaging and path planning, positioning us for mid-teens growth in high-acuity areas. Supply chain digitization at sites like Guadalajara and Galway supports 95% capacity for key catheters and implants.

Next, Lisa with insights on our commercial strategy.

Lisa Moreno:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. Our commercial team has been instrumental in driving adoption of our products. We are focused on expanding our market presence and enhancing customer engagement through targeted sales force expansion—over $500 million invested in direct-to-hospital efforts in the U.S.—and key account programs like Utilization Accelerators with Mayo and Cleveland Clinic, lifting attach rates to 95%.

We've secured GPO wins, NHS value-based deals, and JVs in China with Mindray, ramping EvoClip and NeoFlex to capture 10-15% shares. ASC penetration now at 45% for orthopedics, with bundling of AI software and robotics. Emerging markets see doubled volumes in India via affordable bundles, and we're leveraging regulatory wins for rapid commercialization. This drives 12-14% U.S. growth and positions us for outperformance.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Lisa. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: Press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Alex, on the recent FDA approvals like AetherFlex TAVR, could you provide more color on the expected launch timeline and initial market share capture in the U.S.?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. Great question. As I detailed earlier, AetherFlex PMA allows Q4 full commercialization, with early-access sites already underway. Based on IDE data's superior outcomes—92% success, 35% less leak—we're targeting 15% U.S. share ramp from current levels, starting with 8,000 procedures in Q4 via 500 surgeon trainings. LOIs with top IDNs position us for $250 million FY2025, building on modular design efficiencies.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Hi, thanks. Jennifer, regarding organic growth, how sustainable is the acceleration in APAC, particularly China, and any updates on segment mix shifts?

Jennifer Hale:
Thanks, Emily. APAC's 12.4% organic is durable, led by 25% China post-TAVR approval adding $45 million, despite regs—our Mindray JV ensures localized ramps. Japan/India add via CGM/endo. Segment-wise, Cardiovascular's 11.5% leads, but expect Ortho/Neuro convergence to 10-12% into FY25 as Mako util hits 85% and ReviDBS breakthrough drives. Mix stable at 42/25/18/15%, with high-acuity pull-through sustaining.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Good morning. Lisa, on commercial strategy, with pricing pressures ex-U.S., how are you driving adoption of premium products like EvoClip and robotics in EMEA and APAC?

Lisa Moreno:
Thanks, David. We're countering pressures with value-based models—92% payer acceptance in Europe tying neuro to outcomes, adding €45 million. EMEA NHS/Germany tenders bundle AI with EvoClip for flat-to-up ASPs despite MDR. APAC local manufacturing via Mindray/JVs mitigates tariffs, doubling India volumes; robotics ASC push lifts 35% penetration. Sales productivity +12% via CRM/digital sims supports 14% U.S./12% APAC growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim:
Thanks. Dr. Patel, for the technology roadmap, what's the status on AI integrations across TAVR and neuromodulation, and R&D ROI expectations?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Appreciate it, Rachel. AI is core: TAVR deployment analytics cleared as SaMD Level 2, cutting leaks 30%; NeuroLink/NeuroStim real-time algorithms reduce battery 40%, Phase III migraine data 65% responders. NVIDIA GPU path planning rivals da Vinci, boosting util 30%. $1.2 billion FY R&D (10-22%) yields 12 launches, modular Lego design -28% time-to-market; ROI via 75% margins on leadless like PulseGuard, targeting mid-teens segment growth.

Operator:
Thank you. 

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are dedicated to driving innovation and delivering value to our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
